channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Apple Pay and Google Pay for Digital Payments
item.description: Uzbekistan has officially launched Apple Pay and Google Pay, marking a significant change in the country's digital payment landscape. This development follows a meeting in September between the Head of the Presidential Administration and Google's Vice President, Karan Bhatia, where YouTube monetization was also discussed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Electricity Consumption Surges 34% Amid Cold Snap, Energy Sector Warns
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has seen a 34% surge in electricity consumption, reaching over 64 million kWh on October 27th, a level typically seen in December. National Electric Network of Kyrgyzstan attributes this to widespread use of electric heaters due to the cold weather. This increased load raises the risk of overloads on the energy system.

item.title: Tajikistan Conference Proposes Measures to Strengthen Protection for Human Trafficking Victims
item.description: A conference in Dushanbe on October 22nd discussed strengthening legislation and protection for victims of human trafficking. Organized by the Interdepartmental Commission for Combating Human Trafficking, the event included legal experts, academics, and international organizations. Key discussions focused on improving legal frameworks and ensuring non-punishment for victims exploited through coercion.

item.title: European Natural Gas Prices Surge to Record Highs Not Seen Since Late 2022
item.description: Natural gas prices in Europe have reached levels not seen since late 2022, driven by the halt of gas transportation through the Strait of Hormuz and the start of the heating season. Reuters reports that Iran's attacks on ships and low gas reserves in European storage have complicated the market.

item.title: Tajikistan Establishes Aid for Repatriation of Deceased Migrants' Bodies
item.description: Tajikistan has for the first time formalized assistance for the repatriation of bodies of deceased migrants. This initiative aims to provide support to families dealing with the loss of loved ones who passed away while working abroad. The specific details of the aid and the process for accessing it were not immediately available.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Tax Reform Effectiveness Questioned Amidst Business Closures
item.description: Over 356,000 individual entrepreneurs in Kazakhstan closed their businesses this year, a 59.3% increase from last year. However, Minister of National Economy Serik Zhumangarin stated that evaluating tax reform solely based on closure numbers is misleading. Many closures are due to shifts to special tax regimes or lack of activity, not necessarily reform failure.

item.title: Remote Badakhshan Districts Suffer Severe Healthcare Shortages, Forcing Patients to Seek Treatment Abroad
item.description: Residents in Badakhshan's border areas report critical shortages of health centers, specialist doctors, and medicine. Difficult travel and long distances to facilities mean some patients must go to Tajikistan for care, with some dying en route. Economic hardship and poor roads exacerbate access issues, leaving many without essential medical services.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prime Minister Demands State Body Coordination to Combat Domestic Violence
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov chaired a meeting on implementing the 'Law and Order' principle, emphasizing its importance for national goals. He highlighted that 2,000 Kazakh citizens are at risk of domestic violence. The meeting focused on coordinating state bodies to prevent offenses and promote a culture of lawfulness and public safety.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Cover Mortgage Payments for 500 Young Medical Workers Annually
item.description: Uzbekistan will cover 25% of the initial mortgage payment for 500 young medical professionals each year. Additionally, next year, the government will assist 1,000 healthcare workers with at least 15 years of service in obtaining housing.

item.title: Trump Telegrams Tokayev, Anticipates Meeting at G20 Summit
item.description: US President Donald Trump sent a telegram to Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, congratulating him on Republic Day. Trump expressed pride in the deepened partnership between the US and Kazakhstan, highlighting cooperation in international peace, security, and commercial agreements. He anticipates meeting Tokayev at the G20 summit in December.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Licensing for Medical and Pharmaceutical Staff by July 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan will begin state registration for medical and pharmaceutical personnel on July 1, 2027. Registered doctors and pharmacists will receive bonuses. Initially voluntary, the licensing will become mandatory from 2030. This reform aims to ensure only professionals practice medicine and pharmacy, with bonuses of up to 7 million soms for doctors and 3.5 million soms for nurses.

item.title: UK Prince William Praises Kazakhstan's Efforts in Saiga Conservation
item.description: Prince William of the UK highlighted Kazakhstan's success in restoring saiga antelope populations on The Graham Norton Show. He noted the crucial role of state support in preserving the species, which was once on the brink of extinction. The 'Golden Steppe' initiative, part of this effort, won an Earthshot Prize in 2024.

item.title: Dollar Demand Decreases in Kazakhstan Despite Favorable Exchange Rate
item.description: In September, net dollar purchases in Kazakhstan's exchange offices fell by 29% to 100 billion tenge, despite the dollar reaching a favorable rate of 440.49 tenge. This decline suggests market saturation, with many having already converted savings. Almaty saw the highest demand, followed by Shymkent and Astana.

item.title: Uzbekistan Implements Dual Education System to Enhance Graduate Employability
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing its higher education system by implementing a dual education model, combining university studies with practical workplace training. This initiative, guided by a presidential decree, aims to equip graduates with essential practical experience, addressing the common challenge of a lack of work experience among new graduates. The program allows students to apply theoretical knowledge in real-world professional settings.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economy in 2027: Analysts Predict Tenge Depreciation Amidst Lower Oil Prices and Interest Rates
item.description: Analysts forecast that Kazakhstan's tenge may weaken against the US dollar by 2027, reaching 515 tenge per dollar. This projection is based on the gradual decrease in the base interest rate and potential decline in oil prices. While the tenge strengthened in Q3 2023, future factors like reduced National Bank currency supply and lower rates are expected to influence its course.

item.title: Criminology: A Scientific Tool for Building a Safer Society in Uzbekistan
item.description: Criminology is presented as a crucial science for understanding and preventing crime in Uzbekistan. Unlike criminal law, which focuses on punishment, criminology investigates the root causes and trends of criminal activity. The article emphasizes that crime prevention requires a multi-faceted approach involving not only law enforcement but also community organizations, educational institutions, and families.

item.title: Criminal case opened against Astana kindergarten teacher after child's severe burns
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated against a kindergarten teacher in Astana after a one-and-a-half-year-old child suffered severe burns from hot soup. The child sustained third-degree burns affecting 10% of their body. The mother claims the kindergarten administration initially refused to provide surveillance footage, but police have since seized the recordings for investigation.

item.title: National Bank of Kazakhstan launches website to identify fraudsters and prevent financial scams
item.description: The National Anti-Fraud Center, under the National Bank of Kazakhstan, has launched antifraud.kz. This portal allows citizens to check suspicious websites and investment companies, and find information on how to protect themselves from financial fraud. It includes information on fraud schemes, a directory for checking dubious resources, and an AI assistant named 'Froddy'.

item.title: President Tokayev issues several instructions to the Chairman of the Supreme Court
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has given a number of instructions to the Chairman of the Supreme Court. The specific details of these instructions were not provided in the source text.

item.title: Creator of Financial Pyramid 'R.O.I.' Arrested in Almaty; 275 Victims Identified
item.description: The organizer of the financial pyramid 'R.O.I.', which operated as a consumer cooperative, has been arrested in Almaty. The Financial Monitoring Agency reported that 275 citizens have been recognized as victims, suffering losses totaling 217 million tenge. Organizers allegedly funneled 94 million tenge to affiliated entities under the guise of consulting fees.

item.title: International Crypto Exchange Kraken Secures Preliminary Approval in Kazakhstan
item.description: Global cryptocurrency exchange Kraken has received preliminary approval from the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC) regulator to operate in Kazakhstan. The company also signed a memorandum of cooperation with the Ministry of Digital Development. This move is expected to boost Kazakhstan's digital asset market and its position as a regional crypto hub.

item.title: Fifth Plenum of China's Communist Party Central Committee Opens in Beijing
item.description: The fifth plenum of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China commenced in Beijing on October 26. General Secretary Xi Jinping presented a report on the Politburo's work and explained a draft decision on strengthening party self-governance and discipline.

item.title: Kazakhstan Government Reallocates Budget Funds, Increasing Defense Spending
item.description: The Kazakh government has reallocated budget funds, resulting in a 41 billion increase for the Ministry of Defense. Conversely, social protection funding has decreased by 55 billion.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Abolish Regions and Districts, Create Over 20 New Districts
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to abolish its current regions and districts as part of the second phase of its administrative-territorial reform. Over 20 new larger administrative units, called aimaks (districts), will be created. This reform aims to consolidate districts and eliminate overlapping governance functions, with the first phase having already reduced the number of rural districts.

item.title: Tajikistan's Fixed Capital Investment Increases by Nearly 45%, Energy Sector Leads
item.description: Investment in Tajikistan's fixed capital has surged by nearly 45%. Over half of these investments are directed towards cities and districts under the republic's jurisdiction. The energy sector has attracted the largest share of this investment, indicating a significant focus on its development.

item.title: Uzbekistan Issues First Islamic Banking License to Open Bank
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has issued its first license for Islamic banking activities to Open Bank. The license, granted on October 23, 2026, allows the bank to offer financial services compliant with Sharia principles, including profit-sharing and leasing, while prohibiting interest-based transactions.

item.title: Nearly 90 Percent of Bishkek Infectious Disease Hospital Patients Are Children
item.description: The Republican Clinical Infectious Diseases Hospital in Bishkek is currently treating 373 patients, with children making up 86% (321 individuals). The hospital head doctor stated that around 250 patients seek treatment daily, with 70-80 having acute respiratory infections. The facility has 500 beds and is not overcrowded. The Ministry of Health anticipates a peak in respiratory illness cases by late November.

item.title: 105 Apartments Available for Purchase with Affordable Mortgages in Almaty
item.description: Almaty will begin accepting applications on October 29 for 105 apartments in the 'Zhas Qanat' residential complex under an affordable mortgage program. 'Otbasar Bank' offers loans with annual interest rates not exceeding 2% or 5%. Applicants need at least 10% of the loan amount in their savings account. Applications are open until November 9.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seizes 5.6 Million Liters of Illegal Alcohol, Volumes Rise Eightfold
item.description: Kazakhstan has seized 5.6 million liters of illegal alcohol in the first nine months of the year, an eightfold increase compared to the same period last year. The government reported violations in accompanying documents and underground production with counterfeit excise stamps. Police also noted a decrease in alcohol-related crimes.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes 200,000 Som Fee for Foreign Companies Opening Bank Accounts
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a proposal to charge foreign companies 200,000 som for accreditation to open and service accounts in local commercial banks. The Ministry of Economy and Commerce developed the draft resolution to implement changes in the non-tax revenue code. The initiative aims to create transparent rules and reduce risks of money laundering and terrorism financing.

item.title: Nearly 70 Percent of Kazakh Citizens Trust the Country's Judicial System
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Supreme Court Chairman Aslambek Mergaliyev. The President was briefed on the judicial system's performance over nine months, digitalization efforts, and measures to enhance public trust. Trust in the system rose from 55.2% in 2023 to 69.7% currently, according to the National Statistics Bureau.

item.title: Kazakh Activist Sanjar Bokayev Faces Trial Over Corruption Remarks
item.description: Kazakh activist Sanjar Bokayev is on trial in Almaty, facing five criminal charges following an interview where he discussed corruption and nepotism within the country's state apparatus. Observers have raised questions about the trial, which began in March 2026, shortly after his arrest in August 2025.

item.title: Police Launch Investigation into Tree Felling in Almaty
item.description: Almaty police have opened a criminal case following the felling of trees along Baitursynov Street. Videos of workers removing greenery circulated on social media, with speculation of a residential complex being built. The environmental police are assessing the damage, and the land is privately owned. Authorities have not disclosed construction plans.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Genetic Testing in Collaboration with Harvard
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce genetic testing and train specialists in hereditary diseases in partnership with Harvard Medical School. The country will also establish a legal framework for bioethics and biotechnology. This collaboration aims to advance medical research and healthcare within Uzbekistan.

item.title: Tajikistan and EBRD Discuss $900 Million Investment Roadmap
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon met with EBRD Vice President Matteo Patrone to discuss cooperation and investment. The EBRD has been a key partner since 1993, with over 1.1 billion euros invested in 201 projects. A new roadmap for 2026-2030 outlines $900 million in strategic investments, focusing on green energy and infrastructure modernization.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce New Allowances for Medical Personnel Up to 5.5 Million Soums
item.description: Uzbekistan will reform its medical education system and introduce new allowances for healthcare workers, announced President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Starting in 2027, students will gain clinical experience, and graduates will complete full internships. Allowances will range from 1.5 million to 2.5 million soums for various categories of medical staff.

item.title: Global Oil Prices Decline Amid Middle East Diplomatic Efforts to Ease Tensions
item.description: Global oil prices have fallen as diplomatic initiatives in the Middle East aim to de-escalate regional tensions. Following a meeting in Tehran attended by Iranian, Saudi, Turkish, and Pakistani representatives, Brent crude futures dropped to $115.15 per barrel and WTI crude to $101.32. The price decrease reflects reduced market concerns over potential oil supply disruptions.

item.title: Afghanistan Urges UN and International Community to Act Against Drug Production in Pakistan
item.description: Afghanistan's Ministry of Interior Affairs has called on the UN and the international community to condemn drug cultivation and production in Pakistan, particularly in Balochistan. Ministry spokesperson Abdul Mateen Qani stated that drugs produced in Pakistan are of low quality and harmful. He urged international bodies to take action against drug trafficking.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement 10 AI-Based Systems in Healthcare, President Announces
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to introduce 10 new artificial intelligence-based systems in the healthcare sector, President announced. These systems will enable remote patient monitoring and disease detection through speech analysis, expanding the use of modern technologies for doctors.

item.title: Tajikistan Presents Investment Opportunities at Forum in Qatar
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Economic Development and Trade, Zavqizoda Zavqizoda, participated in a ministerial roundtable at the World Investment Forum in Doha, Qatar. He highlighted investment opportunities in hydropower, mineral processing, textiles, agricultural processing, and high value-added production.
